name: James Woodford
title: Ph.D. Student
bio: I am a Ph.D. student in Mechanical Engineering at the University of Alberta, working in the Energy Systems Design Laboratory. I build numerical methods and simulation software for electrochemical energy devices, from 3D reconstructions of porous electrodes to the finite element solvers that run on them. My goal is to make pore-resolved simulations fast enough that modelers no longer have to trade physical fidelity for tractability.

research_interests.title: Scalable Numerical Methods
research_interests.description: Finite element discretizations, preconditioners, and parallel/GPU solvers for the large, stiff, nonlinear systems that pore-resolved models produce.

research_interests.title: Electrochemical Interfaces & Transport
research_interests.description: Microscale models coupling interfacial reaction kinetics with charge and multiphase mass transport in catalyst layers and porous electrodes.

research_interests.title: Image-Based Modeling
research_interests.description: Turning PFIB-SEM tomography into simulation-ready microstructures, so models reflect the materials that are actually made.

news.text: Presented Impact of varying ionomer coverage on water intrusion, mass transport, and electrochemical performance in PEMFC catalyst layers via 3D microscale modeling at the 250th ECS Meeting.
Started my Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering at the University of Alberta.
Preprint with J. Mouallem et al.: Quantifying causes of voltage loss in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis.
Our work on multi-scale computational analysis of cathode catalyst layers was presented as an invited talk at the International Workshop on Fuel Cell MEA, Fraunhofer ISE.
Published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Unveiling the role of PTFE surface coverage on controlling gas diffusion layer water content.
Presented work on PTFE coverage and gas breakthrough in gas diffusion layers at the 5th annual NSERC CREATE ME² conference.
Published in ChemCatChem: Strong metal-support interactions in ZrO₂-supported IrOx catalyst for efficient oxygen evolution reaction.
Co-authored an abstract on Ir oxide catalysts on different supports at the 242nd ECS Meeting.
Received an NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award to work in the Semagina Lab.
